newsitem.title: USA: Widow sues Continental over husband's death.
newsitem.headline: Widow sues Continental over husband's death.

text.p: The widow of a retiree who died after having a heart attack on a flight to the Bahamas sued Continental Airlines on Tuesday, alleging the plane should have made an emergency landing, her lawyer said.

The lawsuit, filed on behalf of Carolyn McDowell, sought in excess of $10 million in damages and accused the airline of gross negligence in the death of her husband of 22 years, retired businessman John McDowell, said Tod Aronovitz, a personal injury attorney in Plantation, Florida.
Continental declined to comment, because it had not been served with the lawsuit, a company vice president said.

McDowell, 59, a resident of Upper Montclair, New Jersey, who had worked for EDS Corp., was a passenger on a Continental plane en route from New Jersey to Nassau, the Bahamas, for a family reunion May 18 when he suffered a heart attack off the coast of Jacksonville, Florida, Aronovitz said.

A cardiovascular surgeon aboard the plane performed cardiopulmonary resuscitation, administered oxygen and medication, and told the crew the aircraft should be diverted immediately to the nearest airport, he said.
"They never landed the plane in Jacksonville, Orlando or Fort Lauderdale, as advised, but continued to Nassau," Aronovitz said.

The lawsuit, filed in a Broward County, Florida, circuit court, also claimed that the pilot did not properly inform physicians on the ground in Nassau of the nature of the emergency. As a result, the ambulance that awaited the plane was ill-prepared to deal with a heart-attack patient, the suit said.
McDowell was alive when the plane landed in Nassau but died on the way to a hospital, Aronovitz said.
"What we allege is that Continental had a duty to a ticketed passenger, and as a result of their failure to comply with standard air industry rules and regulations, this man died," he said.
